question: Can a stable, task-diverse benchmark determine whether mechanistic-interpretability methods precisely and concisely recover causal pathways or task-relevant causal variables in language models?

key_findings.claim: MIB is an umbrella benchmark rather than a new interpretability algorithm: it standardizes two complementary tracks, fixed counterfactual pairs, public/private splits, and living leaderboards across natural pretrained models plus one semi-synthetic ground-truth model.
key_findings.evidence: The circuit track ranks component/edge localization methods; the causal-variable track ranks featurizers and feature selectors using interchange interventions. The materials include IOI, arithmetic, synthetic MCQA, ARC, and an incorporated RAVEL setting; four open-weight LMs are used for natural tasks, while an SIIT-trained InterpBench-style IOI model supplies the only labeled natural-language circuit. Users prototype on public tests and submit artifacts for hidden private evaluation.

key_findings.claim: The new CPR/CMD circuit metrics usefully separate task-supporting performance from behavioral resemblance and marginalize the circuit-size threshold, but their normalized faithfulness ratio is unbounded and can be undefined or numerically unstable.
key_findings.evidence: Faithfulness is f(C,N;m)=(m(C)-m(empty))/(m(N)-m(empty)); CPR integrates f over circuit size and CMD integrates |1-f|. The denominator has no stated nonzero-margin condition or stabilization rule, and a circuit can overshoot the full model, which is visible in CPR values above 1 and as high as 3.20. The authors explicitly state that realistic best/worst CPR and CMD values cannot be bounded. Consequently CPR can reward a smaller circuit for outperforming rather than reproducing N, while CMD penalizes the same overshoot; both remain conditional on m and the empty-circuit intervention.

key_findings.claim: The proposed weighted edge count does not make node-, neuron-, and edge-level circuits granularity-neutral; it structurally prices a node as all outgoing edges and therefore favors edge methods under a sparsity-based score.
key_findings.evidence: Equation 2 treats inclusion of a node as inclusion of all outgoing edges and a neuron as the corresponding fraction of those edges. This is neither parameter count, runtime, description length, nor causal degrees of freedom. The paper itself attributes poor node-level performance to this accounting: each node costs many edges and cannot be as sparse as an edge circuit. Thus part of the method ranking is induced by the benchmark's ontology and size convention, not localization quality alone.

key_findings.claim: MIB measures faithfulness to a fixed counterfactual/intervention distribution, not an intervention-invariant natural mechanism; matching discovery and evaluation corruptions is a major source of the reported gains.
key_findings.evidence: All evaluation pairs use author-chosen, fixed counterfactual mappings. Counterfactual-ablation circuits outperform mean and optimal-ablation circuits, and the authors explain this by noting that counterfactual discovery more closely resembles the evaluation setting and more precisely targets the benchmarked distinction. Public/private IOI splits change templates and attributes, but retain the same transformation families. CPR/CMD marginalize over circuit size only, not over corruption generator, ablation family, graph decomposition, token scope, or task shift.

key_findings.claim: For natural pretrained models, high CPR or low CMD is behavioral sufficiency under ablation, not recovery of the true circuit; completeness is unavailable outside one narrow semi-synthetic IOI arm.
key_findings.evidence: The authors say precision/recall would be preferable if the ground-truth circuit were known and include one trained IOI model for edge AUROC. On real models they cannot compute completeness and explicitly acknowledge that complement faithfulness is not a reliable substitute. The semi-synthetic arm is only a six-layer, four-head, d_model=64 IOI model trained for 70 H100 hours; it does not validate natural circuits across the task/model suite.

key_findings.claim: The baseline ranking is not statistically calibrated and is confounded by unequal compute, unequal sample counts, and lightly tuned hyperparameters.
key_findings.evidence: Tables report point estimates with no confidence intervals or significance tests. Only the random circuit is averaged over three seeds; no multi-seed protocol is reported for trained masks, DAS, DBM, or stochastic feature selection. Exact edge activation patching uses fewer examples because of runtime, UGS and exact methods are missing from most larger-model cells, and methods exceeding an arbitrary one-week threshold are omitted. The authors state that baseline hyperparameters were not exhaustively searched; causal baselines use task-dependent epochs, batch sizes, learning rates, and manually chosen DAS dimensions.

key_findings.claim: The headline that supervised DAS beats SAE features and neurons is real for these reported cells, but it is not a controlled featurizer-quality comparison.
key_findings.evidence: DAS directly optimizes an orthogonal subspace using labels from the target high-level causal model, whereas PCA, fixed neurons, and public GemmaScope/LlamaScope SAEs are generic unsupervised representations followed by DBM. DAS dimensions are manually set to 16, 32, one-half, or one-eighth of the residual width depending on variable; no matched capacity, supervision budget, selected-feature count, SAE family sweep, or seed variance is reported. Qwen has no SAE result, and the paper concedes that DAS's win is unsurprising because it is uniquely supervised.

key_findings.claim: The causal-variable track conditions away model failures and tests author-specified variables one at a time, so it evaluates manipulable correlates on successful examples rather than validating a complete algorithm.
key_findings.evidence: Every base example and all counterfactuals on which a model predicts incorrectly are filtered out. The benchmark brute-forces manually selected token locations and reports averages and best layers. Its own limitations say the metric aligns a single causal variable, not the full high-level model, and presumes that the hypothesized graph exists. The MCQA high-level model uses an oracle lookup from input to correct answer position; RAVEL similarly filters failure cases. This prevents evaluation of why the model fails and changes the evaluated data subset across models.

key_findings.claim: The causal-variable leaderboard has no explicit complexity or selectivity control for the featurizer, even though it allows nonlinear features and accepts user-supplied invertible Python mappings; this can make IIA reward expressive remapping rather than human-readable mechanism recovery.
key_findings.evidence: The framework permits neurons, orthogonal directions, SAE features, and nonlinear features. A submission supplies an invertible featurizer, inverse, token-position functions, and learned state, but the paper specifies no description-length, model-capacity, training-label, or negative-control budget. The only baseline control is a full-vector identity map. Because the score checks interventional output equality, an increasingly expressive F can fit the fixed intervention mapping without yielding a concise or independently meaningful causal variable.

key_findings.claim: The paper's arithmetic case study is a useful negative control, but its high-level model is internally inconsistent and its carry signal disappears under the less confounded counterfactual.
key_findings.evidence: Section 4.4 defines carry as 1 when the ones digits sum is greater than 10, incorrectly excluding sums equal to 10; Appendix Figure 9 correctly says carry occurs when the sum exceeds 9. More substantively, counterfactuals differing only in carry make the tens output perfectly correlated with carry and produce an apparent mid-layer signal, whereas random counterfactuals break that correlation and yield total failure. The authors consequently conclude only faint evidence in Llama and chance performance in Gemma.

key_findings.claim: Several specification and reporting contradictions make an independent leaderboard implementation ambiguous despite the benchmark's standardization goal.
key_findings.evidence: The IIA equation on page 7 is an unnormalized sum of indicators even though Appendix F defines IIA as a proportion. Section 3 evaluates ten circuit sizes including k=1, while the portal requests nine submitted circuits (plausibly excluding the known full model) but then says the second-smallest may have k<=0.2 rather than the listed 0.002. Table 17's Random arithmetic row is 0.25,0.25,0.75,0.75 under columns CPR+/CMD+/CPR-/CMD-, contradicting the main averaged CPR=0.25 and CMD=0.75 and the otherwise operator-consistent table. These are likely notation/typesetting errors, but a benchmark contract needs machine-checked invariants.

key_findings.claim: The stated leaderboard aggregation does not solve cross-cell comparability and may reverse the CMD preference unless an unreported sign convention is used.
key_findings.evidence: The paper says it averages the sigmoid of each CPR or CMD value to put heterogeneous unbounded cells in [0,1]. A plain sigmoid is monotone and has no per-cell scale calibration, so it cannot equalize different task ranges. CMD is lower-is-better, whereas sigmoid(CMD) increases with worse CMD; no negation or inversion is described. The dynamic average also changes when users filter models/tasks and can compare methods on different available subsets because expensive baselines have many missing cells.

key_findings.claim: The IOI causal-model target has a sign-description contradiction and is partially self-derived from the same low-level system it is used to judge.
key_findings.evidence: Page 11 describes the fitted target as the logit difference between indirect object and subject. Page 38 instead says it subtracts the indirect-object logit from the subject logit and that positive means the subject is preferred; yet the unperturbed fitted formula 0.048+2.005+0.768 is positive even though successful IOI predicts the indirect object. The causal model is itself fit from interventions on GPT-2's four previously selected S-inhibition heads, after which feature subsets of those heads are evaluated against it. This can quantify disentanglement, but it is not an independent algorithmic ground truth.

key_findings.claim: Within its stated protocol, the empirical result is broad and practically useful: integrated-gradient edge attribution is the strongest scalable circuit baseline, and supervised DAS is the strongest causal-variable baseline, while public/private rankings are stable.
key_findings.evidence: EAP-IG-inputs or EAP-IG-activations achieves near-zero CMD in many natural task/model cells and the highest CPRs in most cells; EAP-IG-activations has the best InterpBench AUROC (0.81). DAS has the highest mean or best-layer IIA/MSE result throughout Table 3, while SAE+DBM generally trails neuron+DBM. Private Tables 15-16 broadly reproduce public rankings. These are credible protocol-conditional comparisons, not evidence that the methods recover intervention-invariant or complete natural mechanisms.

method.core_idea: Treat mechanistic-interpretability evaluation as two artifact-submission problems: rank circuit localizers by size-integrated causal faithfulness, and rank hidden-vector featurizers by agreement between low-level and high-level interchange interventions.
method.mechanism: MIB fixes task datasets, model checkpoints, base/counterfactual pairs, component graphs, and hidden public/private splits. For circuits, a method scores nodes or edges; circuits at a grid of size budgets are constructed, non-circuit components are ablated, and logit-difference faithfulness is integrated into CPR and CMD. A weighted edge count permits nominal cross-granularity comparisons, while one SIIT-trained IOI model supplies edge-AUROC ground truth. For causal variables, a high-level deterministic causal model defines intervention targets; identity, PCA, SAE, DBM, or DAS featurizers map a hidden vector into features, selected features are patched from a counterfactual run, and output agreement is scored by IIA (or IOI logit MSE). Public leaderboards accept code or circuit artifacts and evaluate them on private examples.
assumptions: Fixed counterfactual pairs isolate the behavior of interest and remain representative of relevant intervention distributions.
Ablating non-circuit components with the chosen counterfactual, mean, or optimized values yields meaningful in-distribution counterfactual models.
The logit difference m and empty-circuit baseline define a stable, nondegenerate faithfulness denominator.
Area over the selected ten circuit-size budgets is an adequate summary of the faithfulness-sparsity Pareto curve.
Weighted outgoing-edge count makes circuits built from nodes, neurons, and edges comparable enough to rank jointly.
Task-level behavioral sufficiency is a useful proxy for causal-pathway recovery when natural ground truth is unavailable.
Author-specified high-level causal variables exist in the evaluated model and are meaningful abstractions of its computation.
Conditioning on correct base and counterfactual predictions does not distort the mechanism-discovery question.
Interchange-intervention agreement distinguishes causal representation from a featurizer that merely fits a fixed intervention mapping.
DAS, DBM+neurons, DBM+PCA, and DBM+SAE are comparable despite different supervision, capacity, initialization, and feature budgets.
Public/private splits and a hidden API are sufficient to limit benchmark overfitting over the lifetime of an open leaderboard.
Point estimates and incomplete task/model matrices are adequate to establish a state-of-the-art method ranking.

techniques.role: Defines both circuit ablations and causal-variable interchange interventions using fixed base/counterfactual pairs.
Integrates normalized task-performance recovery over circuit-size budgets; higher is better.
Integrates absolute deviation from full-model faithfulness over circuit-size budgets; zero is best.
Maps node- and neuron-level circuit membership into a fractional outgoing-edge size convention.
Approximates edge indirect effects with activation differences times output gradients.
Improves local gradient attribution by interpolating inputs or layer activations across five steps.
Learns stochastic pruning-mask probabilities under behavior-preservation and sparsity objectives.
Measures whether aligned interventions on a high-level variable and low-level features produce the same output.
Selects standard, PCA, or SAE coordinates using high-level causal-model supervision.
Learns an orthogonal task-supervised subspace whose patched values reproduce high-level interventions.
Provides one small IOI model with a known edge circuit for AUROC-based completeness/localization checking.
Separates visible development data from hidden test examples and executes submitted artifacts centrally.

evaluations.setting: Circuit localization on IOI, arithmetic, synthetic MCQA, ARC Easy/Challenge across GPT-2 Small, Qwen-2.5-0.5B, Gemma-2-2B, and Llama-3.1-8B where tractable
evaluations.metric: CMD over ten circuit-size budgets; lower is better
evaluations.result: Counterfactual EAP-IG variants usually attain CMD near 0.00-0.14, outperforming random circuits around 0.68-0.75; exact and UGS cells are largely absent at scale.
evaluations.baseline: Random, exact edge activation patching, EAP with counterfactual/mean/optimal ablations, NAP, IFR, and UGS

evaluations.metric: CPR over circuit-size budgets; higher is better
evaluations.result: EAP-IG-inputs or EAP-IG-activations leads most cells, with values roughly 0.63-3.20; values above 1 show that the normalized score is not bounded by full-model performance.
evaluations.baseline: Same circuit methods plus random circuits

evaluations.setting: Six-layer, four-head SIIT-trained IOI model derived from InterpBench
evaluations.metric: Edge AUROC against the designated circuit
evaluations.result: EAP-IG-activations scores 0.81, EAP-mean 0.78, UGS 0.74, EAP-IG-inputs 0.71, random 0.44, and exact edge patching only 0.28.
evaluations.baseline: Known edge labels on one semi-synthetic IOI model

evaluations.setting: ARC Easy and MCQA causal variables for answer position and answer token
evaluations.result: DAS leads mean performance (for example ARC Gemma OAnswer 88 with best 94; MCQA Gemma OAnswer 95 with best 97), while full-vector best layers can reach 99-100 but have much lower averages.
evaluations.baseline: DBM on standard dimensions, PCA or SAE features, and full-vector patching

evaluations.setting: Two-digit addition carry variable in Gemma-2 and Llama-3.1
evaluations.result: All methods are weak: DAS is 31 (35 best) for Gemma and 54 (65 best) for Llama; random counterfactuals eliminate the apparent carry-specific signal.
evaluations.baseline: DBM, PCA, SAE, and full-vector patching

evaluations.setting: RAVEL city country, continent, and language variables in Gemma-2 and Llama-3.1
evaluations.result: DAS is strongest across six variable/model cells (means 57-75), DBM is second, and SAE/PCA generally do not improve standard dimensions.
evaluations.baseline: DBM on neurons, PCA and SAE features, plus full vector

evaluations.setting: GPT-2 Small IOI subject-position and subject-token variables in four known S-inhibition heads
evaluations.metric: MSE between fitted causal-model and low-level logit differences
evaluations.result: DAS scores 2.20/2.08 and DBM 2.22/2.35 for position/token; selected full-head subsets score 2.45/2.82.
evaluations.baseline: Full-vector brute-force subsets of the four heads

evaluations.result: Method rankings are broadly similar to public tests, supporting split stability for the fixed counterfactual families but not intervention-distribution robustness.

limitations: Natural-model CPR/CMD cannot measure precision, recall, completeness, or whether the discovered circuit is the true algorithm.
Faithfulness is unbounded and has no specified behavior when the full-minus-empty denominator is zero or small.
Weighted edge count embeds an ontology-dependent penalty that disadvantages node-level localization.
All conclusions are conditional on fixed author-designed counterfactual and ablation distributions.
No confidence intervals, significance tests, rank-stability estimates, or minimum detectable differences are reported.
Expensive baselines use fewer examples or are omitted on larger models, producing an incomplete comparison matrix.
Runtime, GPU-hours, memory, and inference cost are not leaderboard objectives, so a state-of-the-art rank need not be practical.
Causal-variable evaluation drops all model failures, preventing failure-mechanism evaluation and changing the evaluated subset across models.
High-level causal graphs are human-specified and validated one variable at a time; the full algorithm need not be faithful.
No selectivity or arbitrary-mapping control limits the amount of benchmark supervision that DAS or a submitted featurizer can encode.
SAE conclusions cover selected public SAE dictionaries and a DBM wrapper, not the design space of SAE architectures, widths, sparsities, layers, or feature-circuit uses.
The living private test is static and the paper specifies no reusable-holdout protocol, query budget, submission throttling, or retirement policy.
The benchmark covers text-only language models and relatively short answer behaviors, not multimodal, agentic, long-horizon, or safety-critical mechanisms.
Several equations, submission thresholds, table cells, and logit-sign descriptions conflict internally.
The paper does not describe sandboxing/security for executable Python featurizer submissions, although this is an operational rather than scientific limitation.
failure_modes: A circuit can game CPR by overshooting the full model on the chosen logit metric without resembling the full computation.
Near-zero m(N)-m(empty) can make a task cell dominate an average through an unstable ratio.
A method tuned to MIB's corruption templates can win while failing under a new but semantically valid counterfactual generator.
Changing graph granularity can reorder methods because the size penalty changes even when ablated computation is similar.
An expressive invertible featurizer can memorize or encode intervention labels and achieve high IIA without a concise causal representation.
Filtering wrong answers can make a localization method look reliable precisely by excluding the examples where mechanistic understanding is most needed.
Average IIA over layers can reward a representation repeated diffusely across the network, while best-layer IIA can reward cherry-picking; neither alone establishes localization.
A static private leaderboard can gradually become public through repeated adaptive submissions and score feedback.
Missing expensive-baseline cells can let a method's macroaverage reflect an easier subset rather than superiority on matched cells.
Correlated counterfactual outputs can create an apparent causal variable, as the carry example demonstrates, that vanishes under decorrelated interventions.
A fitted high-level target derived from the same model can turn the evaluation into self-consistency rather than independent causal validation.
Incorrect direction handling in the described sigmoid aggregation could make worse CMD values receive larger aggregate scores.
reusable_insights: Integrating a performance curve over a sparsity axis is more informative than selecting one arbitrary circuit threshold, provided the axis and score are stable.
Separate positive task contribution from full behavioral resemblance; CPR and CMD expose different notions that a single faithfulness label obscures.
Publish fixed counterfactual mappings and hidden tests for reproducibility, but also reserve entirely unseen corruption families to test causal transfer.
Pair realistic unknown-ground-truth models with many labeled semi-synthetic controls; neither arm is sufficient alone.
Add negative controls in which the hypothesized causal variable is absent, labels are permuted, or the base model cannot solve the task.
Rank methods on a Pareto surface of faithfulness, completeness, description length, compute, and uncertainty rather than a scalar leaderboard alone.
Use benchmark metamorphic tests: duplicating examples, swapping logit signs, permuting option labels, and inserting the full/empty circuit should preserve known invariants.
Audit benchmark metrics with reseed noise, synthetic quality ladders, intervention perturbations, and rank-stability analyses before treating small score gaps as progress.
Evaluate success-conditioned and failure-conditioned subsets separately so interpretability methods must explain both correct and incorrect behavior.
Control featurizer capacity and supervision explicitly, for example with dimension, Lipschitz, description-length, label-budget, and held-out-variable constraints.
Report worst-group, worst-decile, or adversarial circuit/full-model divergence alongside average CPR/CMD to detect coherent tail failures.
Version private leaderboards and retire or refresh test families after adaptive use; benchmark longevity is an experimental-design problem.
open_questions: Can a circuit metric remain comparable across edge, node, neuron, and learned-feature graphs without imposing an arbitrary ontology-dependent size conversion?
How should CPR/CMD be stabilized or replaced when the full-versus-empty logit margin is small, changes sign, or is not monotone with circuit size?
Do MIB method rankings persist under held-out counterfactual generators, adversarial corruptions, zero/mean/resample ablations, and alternate output metrics?
What confidence intervals and sample sizes are required to distinguish nearby circuit or featurizer submissions on each task/model cell?
Can natural pretrained models be paired with partial ground truth through planted mechanisms, model editing, compiled subnetworks, or formally verified local circuits?
How much IIA can a randomly initialized, deliberately incapable, or label-permuted model achieve as featurizer capacity increases?
What capacity-normalized comparison fairly contrasts supervised DAS, DBM-selected neurons, PCA, SAEs, nonlinear maps, and sparse feature circuits?
Can a benchmark jointly learn meaningful units and dependency graphs instead of separating featurization from circuit discovery?
How should a reusable private leaderboard limit adaptive overfitting while still giving researchers actionable feedback?
Can evaluation include failed predictions and discover why an LM fails without presupposing the correct human algorithm?
Which circuit scores predict downstream utility such as editing, debugging, robustness, anomaly detection, or safety interventions?
Can machine-checkable benchmark specifications eliminate formula/table/code drift and certify that the displayed leaderboard implements the paper's metric?

competitive_landscape.title: InterpBench: Semi-Synthetic Transformers for Evaluating Mechanistic Interpretability Techniques
competitive_landscape.relationship: closest labeled-circuit benchmark and source of MIB's ground-truth arm
competitive_landscape.difference: InterpBench supplies 86 semi-synthetic transformers with designated circuits and edge-AUROC evaluation, including compiled Tracr programs and simplified IOI. MIB uses an InterpBench-style IOI control but emphasizes realistic pretrained LMs, more natural tasks, fixed private tests, and behavioral size-fidelity curves. The tradeoff is exact constructed ground truth versus realistic models whose natural circuits remain unknown.
competitive_landscape.source_version: NeurIPS 2024 Datasets and Benchmarks proceedings version

competitive_landscape.title: Towards Automated Circuit Discovery for Mechanistic Interpretability
competitive_landscape.relationship: early automated-circuit discovery method and evaluation suite
competitive_landscape.difference: ACDC evaluates circuit discovery across IOI, docstrings, greater-than, induction, and compiled tasks using reference-circuit ROC, sparsity, and model-circuit divergence. MIB broadens the model/task matrix and integrates faithfulness across sizes, but ACDC makes clear that only compiled circuits have defensible edge ground truth; MIB still cannot label natural-model circuits.

competitive_landscape.title: Transformer Circuit Faithfulness Metrics Are Not Robust
competitive_landscape.relationship: direct validity challenge to circuit-faithfulness benchmarking
competitive_landscape.difference: Miller, Chughtai, and Saunders show that circuit scores can change drastically with granularity, node-versus-edge choice, ablation value, token scope, intervention direction, ablated set, and output metric. MIB standardizes one protocol and marginalizes over circuit size, but it does not establish rank stability across those other choices; its leaderboard therefore ranks methods conditional on MIB's intervention contract.
competitive_landscape.source_version: arXiv version available on checked date

competitive_landscape.title: Hypothesis Testing the Circuit Hypothesis in LLMs
competitive_landscape.relationship: statistically calibrated alternative for circuit validation
competitive_landscape.difference: This work separates mechanism preservation, localization/necessity, and minimality into explicit hypothesis tests with reference distributions and multiple-testing control. MIB instead produces broad continuous rankings from CPR/CMD and random baselines, with no per-circuit acceptance test, uncertainty, or natural-model completeness test. The two are complementary, but MIB alone cannot tell whether a score gap is statistically supported.

competitive_landscape.title: Adversarial Circuit Evaluation
competitive_landscape.relationship: worst-case complement to MIB's average circuit curves
competitive_landscape.difference: Adversarial Circuit Evaluation searches for inputs that maximize full-model/circuit divergence and finds benign failures hidden by average scores. MIB's private data limits direct hill-climbing but CPR/CMD still average over examples and sizes. Worst-group, CVaR, or adversarial CMD/KL would expose failures that a high MIB average can conceal.

competitive_landscape.title: RAVEL: Evaluating Interpretability Methods on Disentangling Language Model Representations
competitive_landscape.relationship: direct predecessor incorporated into MIB's causal-variable track
competitive_landscape.difference: RAVEL already evaluates featurizers through controlled attribute interchange interventions and introduces multi-task DAS. MIB incorporates its city country/continent/language split, adds models and other variables, and places it in a private cross-method leaderboard. That arm is therefore an extension and integration of RAVEL rather than independent novelty evidence.

competitive_landscape.title: CausalGym: Benchmarking Causal Interpretability Methods on Linguistic Tasks
competitive_landscape.relationship: closest causal-intervention benchmark across model scales
competitive_landscape.difference: CausalGym converts SyntaxGym phenomena into intervention tasks across Pythia 14M-6.9B and finds DAS strong, but also shows it can learn arbitrary mappings and introduces a control-task adjustment. MIB spans broader task types and families but lacks an analogous selectivity control, so its supervised-DAS advantage may partly reflect privileged labels and expressive fitting capacity.

competitive_landscape.title: Finding Alignments Between Interpretable Causal Variables and Distributed Neural Representations
competitive_landscape.relationship: methodological foundation for DAS and MIB's causal score
competitive_landscape.difference: Geiger et al. introduce supervised orthogonal Distributed Alignment Search and interchange-intervention alignment. MIB's causal-variable track standardizes and broadens this machinery rather than inventing it. A fair benchmark still needs supervision-matched baselines, label-budget learning curves, and controls separating causal abstraction from fitting fixed counterfactual labels.

competitive_landscape.title: SAEBench: A Comprehensive Benchmark for Sparse Autoencoders in Language Model Interpretability
competitive_landscape.relationship: deeper SAE-specific benchmark published alongside MIB
competitive_landscape.difference: SAEBench evaluates more than 200 SAEs from seven architectures with eight metrics spanning proxy quality, disentanglement, interpretability, and applications; proxy improvements often fail to transfer. MIB is broader across method classes but tests only selected public GemmaScope/LlamaScope dictionaries through DBM. Its conclusion that SAEs do not beat neurons is consequently conditional on SAE family, layer, selection wrapper, and task.

competitive_landscape.title: The Non-Linear Representation Dilemma: Is Causal Abstraction Enough for Mechanistic Interpretability?
competitive_landscape.relationship: post-publication theoretical challenge to unrestricted featurizer leaderboards
competitive_landscape.difference: Sutter et al. prove that sufficiently expressive alignment maps can make arbitrary networks causally abstract arbitrary algorithms and demonstrate 100 percent IOI IIA on randomly initialized LMs. MIB allows nonlinear invertible features without a stated complexity budget. The result makes capacity, selectivity controls, and negative models essential before treating higher IIA as more mechanistic understanding.
competitive_landscape.source_version: arXiv version available on checked date

competitive_landscape.title: Findings of the BlackboxNLP 2025 Shared Task: Localizing Circuits and Causal Variables in Language Models
competitive_landscape.relationship: post-publication community validation and extension of MIB
competitive_landscape.difference: The shared task demonstrates that MIB is usable as common infrastructure: three teams and eight circuit methods improve circuit scores with ensembles and regularization, while one causal team improves scores with low-dimensional and nonlinear projections. The small participation count limits field-wide conclusions, and nonlinear gains intensify the need for featurizer-capacity controls rather than merely confirming benchmark progress.

competitive_landscape.title: Certified Interventional Fidelity: Anytime-Valid, Adaptive Evaluation of Causal Claims in Mechanistic Interpretability
competitive_landscape.relationship: post-publication statistical layer missing from MIB
competitive_landscape.difference: CIF defines interventional fidelity as an estimand over explicit input and intervention distributions and supplies confidence sequences valid under adaptive sampling; on IOI it finds some apparent method differences are not statistically supported. MIB offers fixed point estimates and hidden tests but no uncertainty or adaptive-evaluation guarantees. Adding CIF-style intervals would make leaderboard score gaps scientifically interpretable.

competitive_landscape.title: Are Sparse Autoencoder Benchmarks Reliable?
competitive_landscape.difference: Chanin audits SAEBench through reseed noise, synthetic ground-truth correlation, and discriminability along training trajectories, finding canonical metrics can fail and nearby SAE variants are hard to separate. Although it audits SAEBench rather than MIB, the same lenses should be applied to CPR, CMD, and IIA; private data prevents direct access but does not establish rank reliability or minimum detectable differences.
competitive_landscape.source_version: arXiv version available on checked date

novelty_assessment.author_claim: MIB is a lasting, large-scale standard for directly comparing circuit-localization and causal-variable-localization methods across tasks and models, with new integrated circuit metrics and private public leaderboards that reveal real field progress.
novelty_assessment.evidence: The paper genuinely contributes a coherent artifact contract, fixed datasets and counterfactuals, public/private evaluation, broad baseline execution, CPR/CMD size integration, a cross-granularity size convention, and an umbrella leaderboard joining method families previously evaluated separately. However, InterpBench supplies labeled circuits, RAVEL and CausalGym precede causal-variable benchmarking, DAS/IIA are established machinery, and SAEBench provides deeper SAE coverage. The study also lacks statistical calibration, intervention-shift tests, natural completeness, capacity controls, and a compute-normalized ranking.
novelty_assessment.reviewer_inference: Novelty is strong as systems integration and community infrastructure, moderate for the CPR/CMD metric package, and limited at the level of interpretability algorithms or causal-validation theory. The protocol-conditional baseline results are useful, and the later shared task confirms operational value. The broader claim that the scores establish real mechanistic progress is not yet supported: realistic ground truth, metric invariance, statistical uncertainty, featurizer selectivity, and adversarial generalization remain unresolved.

reviewer_notes: Read all 39 extracted pages, including methods, equations, all main and appendix result tables, limitations, dataset/counterfactual specifications, submission contract, hyperparameters, and task-specific causal models. Cross-checked twelve adjacent primary sources on official NeurIPS/PMLR/ACL/OpenReview/arXiv records as of 2026-08-23, including pre-MIB benchmarks and post-publication shared-task, causal-abstraction, statistical-certification, and benchmark-audit work. Arithmetic threshold, IIA normalization, submission-size, Table 17 Random row, leaderboard sigmoid direction, and IOI logit-sign issues are reported as contradictions/specification audits, not assumed implementation behavior; code could silently resolve some paper-level ambiguities. No generated projections were rebuilt.
